Measured in a git-archive extraction of HEAD (.pi/Reviewer-1-Scratch/t43), one injection at a time appended to references/Roles.md, `PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_skill_contracts.py -q -k second_reviewer` after each: (A) "A second Reviewer must merge it once the verdict is recorded." -> 1 failed (caught); (B) "Someone who did not pass it must land the branch." -> 1 failed (caught); (C) "The Reviewer who was not the one to verify it applies the change." -> 1 passed (MISSED); variants "The Reviewer who did not verify it applies the change." / "A Reviewer who was not the verifier applies the change." / "The role that did not record the verdict integrates the change." / "An agent that merely read the diff should integrate the change." -> all 1 passed (MISSED); "Somebody besides the verifier must land the branch." -> 1 failed (caught). Regex probe: elsewhere.search("who did not verify it")=False, elsewhere.search("who did not pass it")=True. The negated-guard also cannot see a copular form ("was not the verifier"), and other_reviewer requires the modifier to precede the noun. So the round-3 defect class (a sentence naming somebody other than the verifier doing the merge) is NOT fixed - the pin passes a suite that still ships the retired two-step in a phrasing a doc rewrite can easily produce. OVER-FIRE: none - honest rows hold, full file 74 passed. GATES @6aeb001 all green, measured on a clean git-archive extraction because .pi/WT-t43 carries an uncommitted duplicate `_quoted`/ARCHIVE_QUOTE_LIMIT edit (dirty worktree; NOT on the revision): pytest -q -> 564 passed, 1 skipped; ruff check . -> All checks passed; ruff format --check . -> 135 files already formatted; mypy src -> Success, no issues in 15 files; teamwork.py links -> issues: 0; merge-tree --write-tree main HEAD -> rc=0; branch-side deletions (merge-base..HEAD) -> none (note: `git diff --diff-filter=D --name-only main HEAD` is NOT empty - it lists tests/unit/test_task_graph_integrity.py, but that is main-side: f51bbe2 added it on main after the merge-base 0fb9f1c, the merged tree contains it, and nothing is deleted by the merge). FIX: give `verif` its \w* suffix, add a copular/noun-phrase branch for "was not the verifier"/"did not verify" and "was not the one to verify", and add C + the four variants above to the test as regression cases. | PIN STILL BLIND to the verifier-negation family outside the two verbs the regex hardcodes (tests/unit/test_skill_contracts.py:1160-1165 not_the_verifier only matches not+(pass|verif|review)). At 174018e, extraction to .pi/Reviewer-3-Scratch/t43, inject one sentence into references/Roles.md, run PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_skill_contracts.py -q -k second_reviewer -> 74 passed (MISSED) for: (b) "A reviewer that did not record the verdict integrates the change." (e2) "Once the verdict is recorded, the change is landed by the agent who did not issue it." (e5) "The branch is applied by a reviewer who did not cast the verdict." Cause: the clause has not+<a non-pass/verify/review verb>, so not_the_verifier and other_actor both fail while merging matches. Also (e1) "The Reviewer who merely read the diff lands it." MISSED: no otherness keyword at all, so any actor-anonymous second-actor phrasing is invisible. Caught correctly: (a) who was not the one to verify it; (c) whoever did not pass it; (d) Reviewer other than the verifier; (e4) Somebody besides the verifier. Over-fire all green (AGENTS.md only-role-to-pass/merge, different-role-verifies, wrapped "there is no second Reviewer step", --no-merge docs), full file 74 passed, whole suite 585 passed 2 skipped, ruff check/format/mypy clean, links 0, merge-tree rc=0, no deletions. Defect is confined to the pin: widen not_the_verifier to not+<word>+<any verdict noun/verb> (record|issue|cast|sign|write|give|return|deliver|decide|verdict|ruling|approval|blessing) and add an actor-anonymous branch (whoever|anyone|any one|the one) so (b)/(e1)/(e2)/(e5) cannot ship green again.

- findings history: BLOCKER engine.py:2870: the posix conversion was applied to the published artifact paths (2821,2832) but NOT to the exclusion key archive_rel = str(archive_path(root).relative_to(project)). On Windows that yields docs\Team\Archive.md while a["path"] is now docs/Team/Archive.md, so the equality in the external filter at 2871 is never true and Archive.md is published as an artifact. Proof (PureWindowsPath simulation of both sides): archive_rel = "docs\\Team\\Archive.md", artifacts = [Project.md, Plan.md, Architecture.md, Decisions.md, Archive.md]; on posix artifacts = the same list minus Archive.md. That re-breaks the deliberate guarantee "Archive.md is append-only and must not be pinned" and makes tests/integration/test_command_surface.py::test_ledger_export_does_not_pin_the_append_only_archive fail on windows-latest (it passes on Linux, so CI stays red on Windows with a different test). Fix: archive_rel = archive_path(root).relative_to(project).as_posix(). Non-blocking: test_privacy_scan.py:629 accepts 0o666 on nt - legitimate (Windows has no POSIX mode bits, os.chmod only toggles FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY and a fresh file reads back 0o666) and exclusivity is genuinely pinned by test_reveal_to_refuses_to_clobber_an_existing_file (code==2 + content preserved), but 0o600 can never occur there so assert only 0o666 with that comment. Non-blocking: engine.py:6654 str(path.relative_to(project_of(root))) is the same non-portable class, latent/display-only.

Proof, driving main() with only the two network seams replaced: c._http_get_bytes raising c.HttpError(url,503) -> "R3 DRIFT 1.1.0: tarball unreadable: https://registry.npmjs.org/@nidvue/teamwork/-/teamwork-1.1.0.tgz: HTTP 503" and main() returned 2 only because R4/R5 also failed; with R4/R5 healthy, _emit([...R3 fatal=False...]) returned 1. Cause: scripts/check_release_consistency.py:767 and :776 catch InputError inside the R3 loop and append a finding instead of setting fatal=True. Effect: a network flake or a malformed published tarball is indistinguishable from real release drift, so a CI gate cannot route infra from drift. The checker itself computes 726bc547afc41ead (and its docstring says so), so the committed record contradicts both the contract and the code it documents. Replace with 726bc547afc41ead (verified: no commit in 402 scanned reproduces it). MAJOR 3 - R8 mis-parses the uvx form, flagging correct prose. _channel_claims() takes the token after "uvx --from pkg" as a console script even when it is an ordinary word: "`uvx --from teamwork-agents` is the fastest way to try it." -> [("teamwork-agents","is")]; "There is no `uvx --from teamwork-agents` channel yet." -> [("teamwork-agents","channel")]. Appended to docs/index.md at e0098e8 this yields "docs/index.md:95: channel runs to, which is not a [project.scripts] entry" and ":97: channel runs channel, ..." (false DRIFT). _negated_install() also never matches a uvx/pipx negation, so a line that denies the channel is still a claim. MAJOR 4 - R6 false negative: any line matching FOREIGN_VERSION is skipped whole, so a real project version on the same line disappears. Appending "Install Teamwork 1.0.2 to match python: 3.12.13 in this guide." to docs/index.md at e0098e8 -> NOT FLAGGED (line 95), while the sibling line "Install with npm install teamwork-agents at version 1.0.2 today." is flagged. The skip must be per token, not per line. MINOR 5 - R4 compares GitHub release names against _version_tags(), which keeps only ^vX.Y.Z$, so a legitimate non-semver release tag is reported with a self-contradicting message: with v1.1.3-rc1 created and a release {"tag_name":"v1.1.3-rc1"}, R4 -> DRIFT "release v1.1.3-rc1 has no tag v1.1.3-rc1 in git tag -l" although git tag -l lists it. MINOR 6 - tar extraction guard is name-only (scripts/check_release_consistency.py:326-331) and relies on extractall defaulting to the safe filter. That default arrives in Python 3.14 (PEP 706); the CI matrix tests 3.9, so on 3.9-3.13 a symlink member with linkname ../../.. passes the guard. ## T-0010 · M9-O: the R8 rule must not flag a risk row that warns against a wrong install channel Measured on commit e0098e8: the offline R8 scan reports 'DRIFT docs/Team/Risks.md:17: channel names teamwork, the project ships teamwork-agents'. That row is risk R-8, whose whole point is that the name teamwork on PyPI belongs to another project, so the line names the channel in order to warn against it - it is not an advertisement. R8 exists to catch an advertised channel that would not resolve, not a sentence that quotes a bad channel as a hazard. As written, the checker makes 'make ci' fail on correct prose and the only escape is to delete the warning or misuse a marker meant for another meaning. Decide the narrowest correct fix and implement it with a test: either extend R8's existing negation handling (it already ignores 'there is no pip install and no venv') to a channel line inside a warning/negation context, or scope the channel-line match to lines that present the command as advice. Do not weaken the rule for a genuine advertisement: a test must still prove that an unmarked 'pip install teamwork-agents' line on a non-PyPI channel is DRIFT. Note: R8's tokenizer is being reworked in the same file (task T-0005 round 3), so coordinate on the file - work on branch developer-1/t-0005 is the owner's; if you need a separate branch, state the base sha you used and keep the edit minimal and conflict-free. - findings history: BLOCKER 1 - adding `push: tags: ["v*"]` makes the new job exit 1 on every tag push, by construction. ci.yml:33 adds tags to the push trigger and ci.yml:321-351 release-consistency has no `needs:`/`if:`, so the job runs on a tag push and checks out the tagged commit (HEAD == the tag). R2 then requires HEAD version STRICTLY greater than every tag, which R1 already forbids (R1 requires version.py AT the tag == the tag). Measured: fresh clone of this repo + `git tag v1.1.2` at main (version.py = 1.1.2), `git checkout v1.1.2`, `python scripts/check_release_consistency.py --offline` -> exit=1, "R2 DRIFT HEAD version 1.1.2 is not greater than tag v1.1.2", "# release consistency: 9 problem(s)". Same at v1.1.0/v1.0.2/v1.0.0 (exit=1 each). So any state where R1 passes guarantees R2 fails at its own tag: the commit comment at ci.yml:30-32 ("the gate must also see the tag that was just created") describes exactly the condition that reddens it. This blocks M9-G (tag v1.1.2) and every future release tag. Fix needs a joint decision: drop the tag trigger, or make R2 exempt the case HEAD is exactly the tag under test, or run the gate on the preceding branch push only. Contract owner is Architect (Architecture.md has no section 11 on main yet, so the frozen text cannot arbitrate). BLOCKER 2 - the revision contradicts the frozen contract it cites. ci.yml:3 says "Contract: docs/Team/Architecture.md (section 9)". Architecture.md:216-217 (on main) still says "On `push` the prose and media paths are `paths-ignore`d", and Release.md:60 says "`ci.yml` therefore declares `paths-ignore` for the prose/media set". Both are now false: `grep -n paths-ignore .github/workflows/ci.yml` on 3340f46 -> no match. The deliverable changes the trigger policy without amending the two documents that define it, and this class of prose-vs-workflow drift is exactly what R6/R8/R9 do not detect. Either Architect amends section 9 (ADR + decision) or the trigger change is reverted. docs.yml:5-6 is stale in the same way ("`ci.yml` ignores documentation-only paths"). MAJOR 3 - the online half is never run by anything. The job comment at ci.yml:335-336 says "The online half belongs in the release workflow or a manual run", but `grep -n check_release_consistency .github/workflows/release.yml` -> NONE FOUND. R3/R4/R5 (npm registry, GitHub Releases) are SKIP in every automated run, i.e. npm-tarball/tag/Release agreement - the original M9 motivation - is unenforced in CI. Task text permits omitting it, so not the fail reason, but it needs a follow-up task, not a comment claiming a home that does not exist. MAJOR 4 - acceptance criterion "It must ... be listed in the required checks" is unmet and unaddressed. `gh api repos/Nidvue/Teamwork/branches/main/protection` -> strict=true, 15 contexts, none matching "release consistency (offline - docs + tags + version)". No follow-up task records who will add it. MINOR 5 - scope step fail-open on a multi-commit push when `before` cannot be resolved. ci.yml:99-105 falls back to `git diff HEAD^ HEAD` (or `diff-tree --root`), which only inspects the LAST commit. Measured in a sandbox with commit1=src change, commit2=docs-only, BEFORE_SHA=40 zeros (new branch) or an unresolvable sha (post-rewrite): code=false, so the 3x3 matrix and every other gated job skip although code changed in the range. Reviewer-1: 'git clone --depth 1 --branch v1.1.2 -> R1 ok 1 tag(s) + R2 ok ... 0 tag(s)'. Required: (1) add fetch-depth: 0 to the release.yml checkout so the gate sees every tag; (2) run the checker --online in release.yml (the job already holds a release token) so R3/R4/R5 stop being permanently SKIP, or record a measured decision why not; (3) prove the gate's exit code propagates - non-zero must fail the release job, not be swallowed; (4) fix the ci.yml:3 header citing Architecture.md 9 for path filtering (Architecture.md:216-217 and Release.md:60 still claim paths-ignore exists). - findings history: FAIL @7bcd30e (Reviewer-4). 4 MAJOR + 3 MINOR. The 3 structural requirements of the task are met and measured: fetch-depth: 0 on all three checkouts (release.yml:55, :195, :303), the consistency job precedes the publish in the dependency graph (release.yml:188 build needs [consistency], :256 attest needs build, :278 release needs [build, attest]), and the gate's exit code propagates (no continue-on-error, no set +e; the only || true is on the grep -c at release.yml:72, and an empty count correctly becomes 0 -> exit 2). The R5 exemption is narrow (release.yml:155 exact-equality on the published tag only) and the R2 exemption is safe on a tag push because release.yml:102-112 forces github.ref_name to be in git tag --points-at HEAD, so a branch push can never reach the job. What fails is the operational behaviour. MAJOR 1 - the release pipeline is red today on the tree it is meant to release, and the author's own evidence does not say so. The commit message's Result reports only R1/R2 and the three exit codes. The same checker on the same v1.1.2 tree reports 27 problems: R8 19, R6 6, R2 1, R9 1. Nineteen of them are "PyPI HTTP 404, the channel does not resolve and is unmarked" (README.md:116,119,122, docs/Team/Decisions.md:121, docs/Team/Release.md:116, docs/guide/install.md:108,124,134,167,177,186), because this project deliberately does not publish to PyPI (docs/Team/Release.md:127 "teamwork-agents is not on PyPI") while the README still advertises `pipx install teamwork-agents` / `uvx --from teamwork-agents` / `pip install teamwork-agents` unmarked. The gate correctly refuses to release that; the consequence is that no release can ship until that prose is fixed (ceo T-0061) or the lines are marked with the contract's channel-unavailable marker. Required: state this in the task's self-check/evidence and name the task that clears it, or scope the release gate to the tag rules (R1/R2/R4/R5) and leave the prose rules to ci.yml. Shipping a permanently-red release path without saying so is the defect. MAJOR 2 - the post-publish R5 re-check downgrades an unreadable input to a pass, and it contradicts the pre-publish gate on the same input. Measured: a checker that exits 2 (PyPI 503, i.e. an unreadable input per Architecture.md 11.1.1) while R5 is ok -> the post-publish step exits 0, because release.yml:351-360 inspects only the R5 rule and never looks at proc.returncode. The pre-publish gate does the opposite (release.yml:168-170 turns exit 2 into exit 2). Architecture.md 11.1.1: "An unreadable input is never downgraded to a SKIP that leaves the exit code at 0." Required: either honour the checker's exit code in the post-publish step, or record a decision that the post-publish step deliberately checks R5 only, with evidence, and make the two steps agree. MAJOR 3 - the post-publish R5 re-check has no retry, so GitHub's eventual consistency turns it into a false failure. release.yml:287 creates the Release, release.yml:301-308 then re-checks out and queries the releases API once, release.yml:355-357 turns any R5 DRIFT into exit 1. A freshly created Release that has not yet appeared in the releases listing makes the job red AFTER the release was published, with no bound on retries and no way to distinguish "not yet" from "never". The author flagged PyPI 503s but not this. Required: a bounded retry/backoff around the R5 read (and a clear message) before declaring drift. MAJOR 4 - the pre-publish gate blocks the release on an anonymous GitHub API failure the job could have avoided. Measured twice during this review: "R5 SKIP online: GitHub API unreadable: https://api.github.com/repos/Nidvue/Teamwork/releases: HTTP 403" -> checker exit 2 -> the gate exits 2 -> the release is blocked. The API is anonymous by design (Architecture.md 11.1.4, "no credential and no token from the environment", limit 60/h per IP as measured: x-ratelimit-limit 60), while the release job itself holds a GITHUB_TOKEN with contents: write (release.yml:280). The same 403 is what made the author's own PyPI 503 note a smaller problem than it is. Required: pass the job's GITHUB_TOKEN to the GitHub reads, or record a measured decision that an anonymous 403 blocks the release, plus a retry. It also uses substring matching where the pre-publish gate uses exact equality (:155). Delete it or make it a real assertion. MINOR 2 - release.yml:181-182 propagates the checker's raw exit code (`raise SystemExit(proc.returncode or 1)`), so a non-contract code (3+) escapes as a step failure instead of being mapped to 1/2. Map it explicitly. ## T-0002 · Engine: git hooks (in-loop enforcement) + unit tests  (developer)
- date: 2026-10-20
- priority: P0
- owner: developer role (work by: Developer)
- reviewer: Reviewer-1
- task / issue: -
- area: hooks

## T-0006 · The privacy gate false-positives on a relative path  (developer)
- date: 2026-10-20
- priority: P1
- owner: developer role (work by: Developer)
- reviewer: Reviewer-1
- task / issue: -
- area: privacy
- self-check: [pass] Re-read the whole diff of 8888a7c line by line and re-ran the gates at that revision. (1) The defect, reproduced first: git log -1 --format=%B b00861c | grep Harness2 names the path, and the shipped scanner reported one [high/high-entropy-secret] finding on that message; after the fix the same message yields 0 findings. (2) The mechanism I changed: _RE_HIGH_ENTROPY matches 32+ base64-ish characters, so it matched the first 33 characters of '<redacted-high-entropy-secret>' and stopped at the '-' that continues the file name - a path fragment, not a value. The fix looks at the WHOLE token the match was cut from (<redacted-env-secret>), asks whether that token reads as a repository path (_is_path_name: every segment is a name of at most three words with an optional extension and no one-letter fragment) and then whether the match is a piece of a name (cut off inside the token, or CamelCase). A credential is a whole token of random characters: it has too many fragments to read as a name, so it is still reported. (3) The false-negative measurement, which is the part that decides the design: I ran 30000 random base64 secrets (the real shape), 5000 padded base64, 2000 UUIDs, and 30000 ADVERSARIAL path-shaped values built to look like names, in 12 realistic contexts each, and counted how many the gate reports today that the new predicate would stop reporting. The answer is 0 lost in every corpus - including the adversarial one, which is why the predicate needs both signals (path shape AND cut-off-or-CamelCase) rather than path shape alone: path shape alone would have lost 100% of the adversarial corpus. (4) The three new tree findings my first draft introduced are gone: 'token = <redacted-env-secret>(...)' in the scanner and two 'secret = "..."' lines in my own test file were read as env-secret assignments, so I renamed the local to 'whole' and the test locals to 'probe'; the tree scan is back to the exact baseline (FAIL 2, both the pre-existing docs/Team/Archive.md:1161 findings) and my change adds nothing to the tree. (5) The history delta, measured with --json before and after: the ONLY finding removed that lives in a real commit is b00861c - the target. The other 7 removed entries are unreferenced blobs my own git stash left in the reflog, which the --reflog walk reaches; I verified both blob shas with 'git rev-list --objects --all --reflog' (0 hits) and 'git rev-list --all' (not present). (6) Non-vacuity, both directions: removing the _is_path_fragment call turns 2 of the 4 new tests red; the plausible over-broad fix ('exempt every value that contains a slash') turns test_a_secret_that_contains_a_slash_is_still_reported red, so the real-secret side is pinned too and not just the path side. ## T-0009 · The dispute panel is computed at role level, so the neutral seat is locked out of a dispute between two instances of one role  (developer)
- date: 2026-10-21

- reviewer: Reviewer-1

- area: governance
- self-check: [pass] Re-read the whole diff against the four contract points. (1) The party test is per instance: _dispute_party_instances resolves raised_by/against to the exact agent names (a bare role name speaks for every instance of that role, so a party cannot hide behind a role name), and _actor_is_dispute_party decides per actor - so Reviewer-2 is a party while Reviewer-3 is not. (2) A role leaves the panel only when EVERY one of its instances is a party (_role_has_neutral_instance): with Reviewer-1 and Reviewer-2 both in the dispute the reviewer role leaves; with Reviewer-3 free it stays and Reviewer-3 is the neutral seat. (3) A party may never sign or resolve, and the refusal is absolute - --force waives the signature requirement, not the party rule; I deliberately made the resolve-side party refusal unconditional, which closes the dead --force escape hatch the old code left open. (4) No other command's behaviour changed: I ran a six-scenario exit-code sweep of sign/resolve/resolve --force for seven actors against main and every value is byte-identical except the one case the defect names (a dispute between two Reviewer instances with a third Reviewer free: panel ['ceo'] -> ['ceo','reviewer'], Reviewer-3 1 -> 0, and the two parties 1 -> 2). The panel check still runs first in both sign and resolve, so an off-panel actor keeps the message and exit code it always had. The escalate notice now names a concrete non-party instance, because a role on the panel can still be the party. | test: pytest -q @ffa2f03 -> 823 passed, 3 skipped; ruff check . -> All checks passed!; ruff format --check . -> 152 files already formatted; mypy src/teamwork -> Success: no issues found in 17 source files; teamwork.py links -> # issues: 0; non-vacuity on tests/unit/test_dispute_panel_instances.py: revert the panel rule to role level -> 2 failed; drop the every-instance rule -> 1 failed (test_the_reviewer_role_leaves_the_panel_when_every_instance_is_a_party); weaken the absolute party refusal -> 1 failed (test_a_party_instance_can_never_sign_or_resolve); remove the sign-side party refusal -> 1 failed (test_a_party_instance_can_never_sign_or_resolve); restore -> 5 passed

- author evidence: MOOT BY DELIVERY at 46e508d via P-0109 (developer T-0021). The unsatisfiable-gate premise is gone: identity --audit --range HEAD -> '# commits: 699 | problems: 0' and each of the four formerly-bad commits now reports ok: e2adba18bfec ok ReleaseEngineer, 2b31500c7beb ok ProductManager, 11c7f77a535e ok ProductManager, 862e575b7004 ok SecurityAuditor (landed by CEO). Cause: _matches_role_display (src/teamwork/engine.py:3370-3379) accepts the instance-form display name for a canonical role mailbox, and _RE_MERGE_SUBJECT (:3312-3322) accepts plain 'Merge branch'/'Merge commit' integrations, so the --range HEAD fallback the forced-push path takes now passes without a rewrite and without an allowlist. No policy change is needed; an allowlist would now be dead weight that could mask a future real defect.
- reviewer evidence: MOOT BY DELIVERY confirmed independently @46e508d. identity --audit --range HEAD -> '# commits: 699 | problems: 0' (no allowlist, no exemption). Spot-checked the four commits the task named: e2adba18bfec ok ReleaseEngineer <releaseengineer@agents.nidvue.com>; 2b31500c7beb ok ProductManager; 11c7f77a535e ok ProductManager; 862e575b7004 ok SecurityAuditor <securityauditor@agents.nidvue.com> (landed by CEO) - the last one exercised both the display-name helper and the merge exemption. Mechanism: _matches_role_display (src/teamwork/engine.py:3370-3379) normalises spaces on both sides, so the no-space instance form is accepted for a canonical role mailbox; _RE_MERGE_SUBJECT (:3312-3322) accepts 'Merge branch <x> into <y>' and 'Merge commit <sha>'. Judged on policy: the task offered 'bound the fallback' or 'an allowlist', but an allowlist would make four real defects permanently silent and a bound fallback would leave the history unaudited; the implemented tolerance is narrower than either - it accepts a name SHAPE that is a canonical role mailbox, and still fails the same commits if the display is not a role (proven by tests/unit/test_commit_identity.py's unknown-display test, 34 tests). So no allowlist, no policy file, and the task closes as satisfied rather than deferred.

THE FINDING WAS CORRECT AND I REPRODUCED IT BEFORE CHANGING ANYTHING: in a scratch repo with the shipped .gitattributes, 'git lfs install --local' and the shipped 'hooks install', a 1100000-byte pure-ASCII assets/movie.bin committed rc=0 and 'git cat-file -p HEAD:assets/movie.bin' printed the Git LFS spec version line - a 132-byte pointer, with the document absent from the tree; the same probe on a 126-byte text assets/small.bin -> a 126-byte pointer. The gates were silent: is_binary_content -> False, lfs_tracked -> True. So the contract promised 'never pushed into LFS' and the code could not keep it, because .gitattributes routes a file into LFS BY NAME and only a refusal can stop that. I TOOK REMEDY (b) - make the promise TRUE - and not (a) - narrow the text - for a reason I can defend: (a) would document the hole and leave a document unreadable without an LFS client, and the audit would still have called such a file 'exempt'; (b) closes the hole and keeps the promise the team actually wants. WHAT CHANGED: gitutil.lfs_text_mismatch is the new shared predicate - a TEXT file that an LFS pattern captures - and all three gates refuse it: the audit reports it as a finding, 'commit --check-lfs' refuses the commit, the hook's R2 refuses the commit, each with a message naming the mismatch ('this file is text but a LFS pattern captures its name; LFS is for binaries, and a document in LFS is unreadable without a client. Drop the pattern from .gitattributes, or make the content binary'). The check is SIZE-INDEPENDENT, because a text file in LFS is broken at any size - the 126-byte probe proved it - so a threshold-gated version would let the small case through. The predicate asks the same two shared questions the other two do (is_binary_content, lfs_tracked), so the three gates cannot disagree. ONE THING I FOUND WHILE IMPLEMENTING IT: gitutil.lfs_tracked IGNORED the '-filter' opt-out - the shipped .gitattributes carries 'assets/social-preview.png -filter -diff -merge -text' and 'docs/assets/* -filter ...', and lfs_tracked reported the opted-out PNG as LFS-tracked. That is a pre-existing bug, but remedy (b) makes it load-bearing: without the fix, a TEXT brand asset under an opt-out would be reported as a misconfiguration that does not exist. lfs_tracked now reads .gitattributes LAST-MATCH-WINS, as git reads it, and a test pins it. THE CONTRACT NOW PROMISES WHAT IS TRUE: 11.10 has a new row ('Is a text record ever pushed into LFS? - No') and a table of the TWO refusals with their opposite remedies (the threshold: add the pattern; the mismatch: drop the pattern), because a file can hit either and the two must not be conflated; R2 names both; the audit's line reads 'N large text record(s) exempt from the threshold', so 'exempt' can no longer be read as 'safe from LFS'. THE FOUR NON-BLOCKING ITEMS ARE FIXED: N1 - references/Engineering.md now states the rule as the code decides it, including the UTF-16 exception ('a file is binary when its first 8192 bytes contain a NUL byte, EXCEPT a head that decodes as printable UTF-16'), and states the mismatch refusal and the size-independence; N2 - the three dangling 'D-20261021-Architect-1' citations are now 'D-20261021-Architect', and the new entry is D-20261021-Architect-2; N3 - 31060 corrected to 30660 (1079236 - 1048576 = 30660); N4 - the dead stage_text helper is gone, and the case it was written for now has real tests in the LFS scope file. The contrast is measured on the same tree: the pre-fix engine (main) reports "1 large file(s) not LFS-tracked, e.g. docs/Team/Archive.md" and the branch engine reports "LFS rules present; 0 large file(s), all tracked"; a large binary under assets/ is still reported by the branch engine. The scoping in the shipped code is therefore correct in behaviour - the hole is only unprotected by tests (F1), and the rule is applied in only one of three gates (F2). Gates at c46ad35 are all green: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -> 850 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed; ruff check . -> All checks passed!; ruff format --check . -> 155 files already formatted; mypy src/teamwork -> Success: no issues found in 17 source files; python3 scripts/teamwork.py links -> 0 issues (72 markdown files, 335 internal links); python3 scripts/teamwork.py identity --audit --range main..developer/t-0013-the-lfs-audit-demands-a-filter-for-the-t -> 1 commit, 0 problems, author == committer == Developer <developer@agents.nidvue.com>; git merge-tree --write-tree main developer/t-0013-the-lfs-audit-demands-a-filter-for-the-t -> rc 0, tree d8bc410da462fc0b336413d4cb7bdff887485a20 == the branch tree. The diff is minimal and in scope: 2 files, +49 lines, no weakened or deleted tests, no secrets, no build output. - findings history: BLOCKING F1 (the module's headline invariant is a false negative in one direction): tests/integration/test_ci_release_flow.py::test_the_docs_trigger_list_and_the_scope_prose_set_are_the_same_set stays GREEN when a docs.yml trigger entry is DELETED, which is the gate hole the module exists to catch (that path is still classified prose, so the matrix is skipped, and docs.yml no longer triggers: nothing runs for it). Measured at 4fc8b25 in a clean worktree of this tree: remove "- \"AGENTS.md\"" from .github/workflows/docs.yml:26 -> pytest -q tests/integration/test_ci_release_flow.py -k same_set -> "1 passed, 15 deselected"; add "- \"notes.txt\"" to the same list -> "1 failed, 15 deselected", so only the add direction bites. Cause: mismatch_report() builds its probe list from docs_trigger_markers(DOCS_WORKFLOW.read_text()) twice - "shipped" and "markers" both read the same mutated on-disk file, so a deleted entry disappears from both - plus the fixed CODE_PROBES tuple, which contains none of the 11 entries of PROSE in .github/workflows/ci.yml:102 (docs/ assets/ README.md CHANGELOG.md CONTRIBUTING.md SECURITY.md CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md CITATION.cff LICENSE AGENTS.md mkdocs.yml). The "Sample the shipped list as well as the given one" comment only protects text mutants passed through docs_text=/ci_text=, which is why test_the_agreement_bites_when_the_docs_list_drops_an_entry passes while real drift does not. Net effect: the whole prose set is unprobed in the "leaves docs.yml" direction, and the docstring's "a path that leaves one list without joining the other is a hole in one of the two gates" / "dropping one entry from either side must produce a named mismatch" is unsupported. ## T-0014 · CI on the pushed revision 074e856 is RED in all 9 test jobs: tests/unit/test_skill_contracts.py::test_document  (developer)
- date: 2026-10-25
- priority: P0
- owner: developer role (work by: Developer-2)
- reviewer: Reviewer-1
- task / issue: -
- area: test-portability
- self-check: [pass] Root cause: _delete_repository restored only stat.S_IWRITE (0o200) on files AND directories; on POSIX a directory without the execute bit is not traversable, so shutil.rmtree raised PermissionError on .git/info (ubuntu) and .git/refs/.git/objects (macOS) - Windows was green only because chmod there merely toggles read-only. Fix: restore owner rwx (stat.S_IRWXU = 0o700) on directories and owner rw (0o600) on files, skip and never follow symlinks, then chmod the tree root; on Windows those bits still only toggle the read-only attribute it already needed. Added regression test test_delete_repository_restores_traversable_directories (0o500 dir containing a 0o444 file; asserts removal plus the restored owner bits) so the defect is provable on any host. | test: pytest -q tests/unit/test_skill_contracts.py @d812501 -> 86 passed, 0 failed; ruff check + ruff format --check clean. Repro: the new test FAILS on the unpatched helper (spy records mode 128 = 0o200) and passes after the fix.
- author evidence: commit d812501
- reviewer evidence: PASS @d812501 (base main 074e856). SCOPE: git rev-list --left-right --count main...HEAD -> 0 1; git diff --name-only main...HEAD -> tests/unit/test_skill_contracts.py only (59 insertions, 5 deletions), no unrelated change. FIX read: directory_mode = stat.S_IRWXU (0o700) for directories, file_mode = stat.S_IRUSR|stat.S_IWUSR (0o600) for files, both loops guarded by entry.is_symlink() so no link is chmodded or followed (os.walk runs with followlinks=False), and path.chmod(directory_mode) after the walk re-chmods the tree root that os.walk never yields. FAIL-BEFORE: in .pi/worktrees/reviewer-1/tip at d812501 I restored the main helper verbatim and ran pytest -q tests/unit/test_skill_contracts.py -k restores_traversable_directories -> 1 failed: AssertionError refs must regain owner read, assert (128 & 256) = the request was 0o200 for a directory, no S_IXUSR and no S_IRUSR; with that same unpatched helper test_documented_install_produces_tracked_files_not_a_gitlink still passed here (1 passed), which is exactly the Windows-green / ubuntu-macos-red gap. PASS-AFTER: git checkout of the file, then pytest -q tests/unit/test_skill_contracts.py -> 86 passed in 0.84s (new test alone 1 passed); full pytest -q -> 1269 passed, 39 skipped, 0 failed in 843s; worktree clean. GATES, same commands as .github/workflows/ci.yml:194-196: ruff check . -> All checks passed; ruff format --check . -> 191 files already formatted. IDENTITY: identity --audit --range main..d812501 -> 1 commit, problems 0; identity --guard-committer --range main..d812501 -> 1 commit(s) carry a role committer, rc 0; author = committer = Developer <developer@agents.nidvue.com>, the canonical role mailbox this repo policy requires; message shape matches repository history (fix(test-portability): plus Task/Role/Producers/Goal/Deliverable/Why/Status/Result and Acting role trailer). MERGE: git merge-tree --write-tree main d812501 -> 5b9b592d, rc 0, 0 conflicts, branch 0 behind main. LIMIT STATED PLAINLY: this reviewer host is Windows only, so the POSIX half cannot be reproduced here - only CI on ubuntu/macos/windows (ci.yml:312, full pytest) can prove that rmtree no longer raises PermissionError on .git/info/.git/refs; local evidence proves the restored mode intent and that the regression guard is red without it, not the POSIX fault itself. Residual, non-blocking: the is_symlink skip branch has no dedicated test; pre-fix the new test fails as a recorded-mode assertion rather than the POSIX PermissionError, by design.

The concurrency group does not save it: .github/workflows/docs.yml:44-46 is "group: pages-${{ github.ref }}" with "cancel-in-progress: false", so a main run and a tag run are in DIFFERENT groups and neither cancels the other. (2) ATTEST: npm needs [consistency, build, attest] - the unit test that pinned the old two-element needs was corrected with the code, and the release job already needed attest. (3) DRAFT THEN PUBLISH: 'Create GitHub Release (draft ...)' now passes draft: true; the R5 re-check is unchanged below it; a NEW last step runs 'gh release edit <tag> --draft=false' and then reads isDraft back and fails if it is not false. The bypass still exits 0. (4) FORCE - 'hooks install --force' with a foreign stage and no --reason dies naming --reason and touches nothing; with --reason it replaces, and where the project has exactly one team ledger the record lands as action hooks.install, target pre-push, detail 'replaced a foreign hook with --force; reason: ...'. (5) UNINSTALL - removing the shim hands pre-push.teamwork-foreign back to pre-push, so the LFS hook cannot be stranded; status reports the chain only when the installed body actually chains it (proved by a --force replacement beside an orphaned preserved file: status prints plain 'installed'). ## T-0005 · Design the feature-team model: feature records, independent feature split, file ownership per feature, and the reporting ADR  (architect)

- self-check: [pass] Re-read the whole diff. artifact_tree=work_repo(root,cwd) reuses the worktree-aware helper audit_repository already trusts, so the lane's cwd picks the lane's tree and a base-checkout invocation is unchanged. project_trees asks git worktree list (porcelain) and falls back to <team>/Runtime/Worktrees/*/.git so a non-git fixture stays testable; candidates are ranked by depth so a lane nested in the base checkout is never read as the base's copy. - task / issue: -

FIX: one index row per entry (id, owner, date, segment+anchor), or id -> every segment, and make the migration test compare all 322 entry targets, not id presence. An entry appended by a review in month N and merged in month N+1 is repointed in the N segment, so `MERGE_RECORD_NAMES names the current segment and the index, so a merge writes two small files` is wrong for cross-month merges, and a constant cannot name a month-varying file. No command rewrites self_note (task set takes --evidence/--status/--priority/--deps/--title; selfcheck only appends; task archive only closes the task), so the only escape is --force, which turns the gate this PR strengthens into a routine override on every rebased round. ONE MAJOR - the standalone preflight still charges the stored self_note's test line after a rewrite and its printed fix cannot clear it: selfcheck green @c1 with --test "pytest -q @<c1> -> 3 passed" -> commit --amend -> c2 -> task set --evidence "pytest -q @<c2> -> 3 passed" -> preflight developer T-0001 -> exit 1 "the task evidence names @<c1>, which no ref contains (a rebase, amend or reset removed it)" (the sha is in the stored note's test line; _RE_PREFLIGHT_DIGEST strips only the "preflight: PF-... @<rev>" digest); the printed fix "task set --evidence" is already applied, so it cannot clear the finding; only a new selfcheck (exit 0) refreshes the latest section and the next preflight is exit 0. This breaks Architecture.md 14.2 (one record per mistake, ids globally unique across every role's Lessons.md) and leaves ledger lesson.add events whose record is gone, so lesson show/fix can report no lesson or fix the wrong one. Expected: every successful add persists exactly one record with a fresh global id, and the ledger event points at it. Fix: hold a team-wide Runtime/Locks/lessons.lock around the read-allocate-write-and-ledger sequence (re-read inside it, as decisions.lock does), and take the same lock for the Skills.md/lesson writes in skill create; add a parallel-add unit test (the sequential tests cannot catch this).

## T-0032 · Amending a branch after selfcheck permanently poisons the task: self-check notes are append-only and preflight requires every @sha in them to be reachable  (developer)
- date: 2026-11-08
- priority: P1
- owner: developer role (work by: Developer-3)
- reviewer: Reviewer-2
- task / issue: -
- area: preflight
- self-check: [pass] [pass] Reproduced the poisoning first: at main the only reader of a stale @sha was the whole evidence field plus the newest note segment, and neither could be told a revision had been rewritten away on purpose, so T-0013 stayed red after the evidence was re-pointed. Fix: _preflight_evidence subtracts the revisions a record itself marks "superseded" (_RE_SUPERSEDED_REV, both the "@<old> superseded by @<new>" and the "superseded by @<new>: @<old>" order) from both the evidence field and the note, and the note_dangling/note_missing hint now names that repair path. Boundary: a note that merely mentions an old revision without the word superseded still FAILs (test_the_marker_is_what_forgives_a_missing_revision), so the marker is the only forgiveness. Empty case: no @<rev> named -> OK, unchanged. Duplicate/second call: revs are de-duplicated by the sorted set before subtraction, and the subtraction is idempotent, so a re-run preflight reads the same verdict; the note stays append-only, nothing is edited in place. Contract: _preflight_evidence(project, task, extra_text="") keeps its signature and its PreflightCheck return; only the accepted set and the OK detail string ("N marked superseded and not checked") change. Concurrency/shared writes: read-only over git for-each-ref/cat-file plus the task dict; no lock, no write, no ledger entry. Scope: src/teamwork/engine.py (_preflight_evidence + _superseded_revs + the fail hint) and the new tests/unit/test_preflight_superseded_evidence.py; no other module, no docs, no task record. What a hostile reviewer would name: the marker is a textual claim, so it can hide a real dangling sha - the detail line reports every forgiven revision, and the Reviewer still sees them in the note. | test: pytest tests/unit/test_preflight_superseded_evidence.py tests/unit/test_preflight.py -W error @c7c49e8 -> 28 passed | preflight: PF-8b882577a665 @652d490c09b4 (7 checks, 0 failed)

The tail it refuses to extend is itself valid (prev/digest match), so this is not the 'verify-rejected tail' the note bounds itself to. The refusal names two remedies and both no-op on exactly this state: 'ledger verify --reconcile' -> exit 1 'the trail has been altered or truncated' (ledger_verify:2826 only rewrites a cache that is BEHIND); 'ledger repair --by ceo --reason ...' -> exit 1 'nothing to repair: every line parses'; 'ledger repair --force' -> exit 1 as well. Nothing shipped clears an ahead cache, so every later append in that team is refused - the team is wedged with no documented way out, and the message sends the operator in a loop. A lagging cache is healed (good); ahead is the hole. SMALLEST FIX: treat an ahead cache as the lagging one is treated (verify-rejected tail -> refuse; head-only disagreement -> NOTE and carry on, since ledger verify already reports the truncation), OR make 'ledger repair --reason' rewrite an ahead cache and record the truncation as a record, and re-word _refused_append to name the command that actually works for the state it refused. Add one acceptance case per state: refused states must have a shipped recovery. NOT this branch: main d0c4e13 is already red (test_skill_contracts x5 measured on d0c4e13 itself, test_docs_pipeline_flow privacy, test_probe_passes[records], test_traceability_matrix AC-5); the branch's own 27 ledger tests pass, and the 7 new ones are red on main's engine (6 fail) - the fix and its oracles are sound.

A role with no open lessons has nothing for the index to displace, so the 228-byte CEO index is pure growth; the two-line preamble returns only ~120 bytes. The reported deltas -712/-712/-523 are not reproducible: measured -9/-9/+125 on independent identical copies of the same store. -712 is exactly the index byte count, i.e. the number was derived as if the verbose lesson rows were absent from the baseline; the CEO figure suggests a cherry-picked fixture where CEO had open lessons. Also missing: any AC-M22-4 test for a role with zero open lessons (all byte assertions pin Developer-1, which has 5 lessons to displace), so the green suite cannot catch this regression.

N=32 -> run1 PASS peak records=32 pids=32, exits 32/32, rc 0; run2 "# started 0/32", rc 1, refusals "dev-5: no free default slot (cap 32) - left queued for the next wave". After run1 every lane exited (outcome files state=exited exit=0) yet Runtime/Slots/default still holds N .slot files (8 and 32 respectively), so the engine refuses wave 2 while scripts/lane_proof.py:97-108 free_slots() skips "default" and therefore never reports the exhausted bucket: the printed capacity is capacity the engine cannot afford, i.e. F1 in the bucket the engine uses. Secondary: idle_instances doubles between runs (8->16, 32->64) because idle_agents() counts Agents/ dirs the runs themselves create, so the capacity line drifts even when the lane set is fixed. Why the shipped test misses it: tests/unit/test_lane_proof.py:97 test_the_proof_repeats_on_the_same_project uses 3 agents with the default cap 32, so the leaked leases never bind; the acceptance case must run lanes == LaneMax == the default cap twice and assert the same PASS and rc 0 both times (and that Runtime/Slots/default is empty after run1).

Ordering: inbox() sorts by (priority rank, created), pinned by a 5-message test that sends low first and expects urgent,high,high,normal,low. One taker: take() refuses a second instance and a closed message; finish() records the result the sender reads. Delivery without interruption: the packet block is injected in build_packet and pinned by a test that asserts the head, the priority rows and the urgent instruction; message inbox is the same list on demand. Preemption: preempt_urgent() stops the live lane, sets the task paused with the message id (engine.set_task_status, under the role queue lock), records lane.preempt, and the swarm then starts a mailbox lane for any instance with urgent mail that has no live lane; lane resume returns the task to doing. Boundary: an unknown recipient is refused with exit 2 and the known list; an empty mailbox prints 'empty'; a message with no subject or an unknown priority raises before anything is written; a second take is refused; a paused task blocks loop (STATUSES gained paused). Concurrency: every mutation is under Runtime/Locks/mailbox.lock; ids are per recipient and never reused (M-0001 twice in two mailboxes is the test). Scope: the new module, the engine CLI + set_task_status + the paused status, lanes (preempt/resume, packet injection, the swarm pass), one test file, and the docs that describe the contract. Not touched: the ledger format, the task graph, the review gate. - findings history: detects: A team that runs a preemption gets a red stop gate and a red audit gate for a state the change itself defines as legal: the CEO reading loop sees "INVALID STATUS ... status=paused" / "1 task(s) have an unknown status" and is told the tree is corrupt when one task is merely waiting, and a manual status fix would silently undo the preemption. Second, an operator reading the task queue after a preemption finds no record of which message displaced the task, although three documents promise it. Reachable in the supported use of the shipped commands (lane preempt, urgent message, then loop/audit/task read). | BLOCKER 1 - the new paused status is reported as a data-integrity error by the two gates that read statuses. Reproduced at e1184ca in a throwaway project (init --agents ceo,developer-1,reviewer-1 --no-git): task add developer "ship it" --priority P0; task set developer T-0001 --status paused; loop -> "## work in flight ... - INVALID STATUS developer T-0001 status=paused ship it" and blocker "1 task(s) have an unknown status"; audit -> "BLOCKER 1 task(s) have an unknown status". Cause: gate_report work buckets are keyed ("todo","doing","selfcheck","blocked","review") (src/teamwork/engine.py:12656-12660), so every status outside that set and outside ("done","dropped") falls into `invalid`, and open_work never counts a paused task. preempt_urgent sets paused on a real task, so the first preemption turns the team stop gate and the audit gate red with a phantom corruption, and the documented contract is not what ships: SKILL.md 5n says "a paused task blocks loop, so the team cannot close while one is waiting" and references/State.md says "a paused task is in flight, so loop will not report STOP while one waits". Required: treat paused as in-flight work in gate_report (its own bucket or folded into doing, counted in open_work) so loop/audit report it as waiting work and never as an unknown status, and add the test that pins it (task paused -> loop CONTINUE naming the paused task, zero "unknown status" blockers, audit clean). FINDING 2 - the pause note never reaches the task, so the documented "paused with the message id" trail on the task does not exist. set_task_status writes tasks[idx]["note"] (engine.py:805) but render_tasks has no `note` field (src/teamwork/records.py:948-990 writes a fixed field list), so the note is dropped on write: after lane preempt L-0001 --message M-9999 the queue shows "status: paused" and no note line. The message id survives only in the ledger lane.preempt detail and in the run record preempted_by, while SKILL.md 5n, references/State.md and references/Coordination.md all state the task carries the message id that displaced it. Required: either persist the note (a task field the writer emits) or state where the id actually lives, and pin it with a test asserting the queue file after preempt. FINDING 3 (minor) - finish() has no terminal guard: message done on an already-dropped message flips it back to done and overwrites the result (scratch: message done M-0001 --drop -> "dropped: first close"; message done M-0001 --result "second close overwrites" -> "done: second close overwrites"), while take() refuses a closed message and references/State.md documents pending -> taken -> done | dropped. NIT: _lane_resume docstring says "at the status it had before" but hardcodes doing (the parser help says "at doing"); build_packet calls messages.packet_lines twice, re-reading every message file twice per packet; cmd_message re-imports json inside the function. VERIFIED GOOD, do not rework: priority ordering (urgent,high,high,normal,low pinned by test), one taker (second instance and closed message refused), per-mailbox ids never reused, unknown recipient refused with exit 2, the packet block (head, priority rows, task suffix, urgent instruction, +N more, and the on-demand re-read line) placed between Assignments and Read-first, preempt_urgent stopping the lane + pausing the task + ledger lane.preempt, lane resume returning doing, message send/inbox/take/done ledger actions, the swarm urgent-mailbox pass, docs (SKILL.md 5n, references/State.md, references/Coordination.md) read against the shipped CLI surface, ruff/mypy clean, branch mergeable (merge-tree rc 0), and the packet probe verified end to end on the live team.

Boundary: capture fires only on a LIVE->terminal transition in lanes.refresh (a non-LIVE run returns before it), and it writes only Roles/<Role>/ShortTermMemory.md through engine.memory_session(strict=False) plus one memory.add ledger event; nothing else is written. Empty case: a lane with no LANE-RESULT line writes nothing (unit test test_capture_skips_a_lane_without_a_lane_result) - the lane.finish record already carries exit/result, so nothing is invented; an empty short store prints no heading and no block at all (test_short_block_is_empty_and_headingless_on_an_empty_store), and short_bytes returns 0 so the pack keeps the full remainder. Duplicate case: an entry whose src equals the task is the agent own note, so the harness does not echo it (test_capture_does_not_echo_the_agents_own_note), and a second reconcile of the same run is a no-op because the first entry now carries that src (test_capture_is_idempotent_for_one_run) - refresh therefore writes at most one entry per (run, task) however often it is called. Second call: short_block/short_entries are pure over the store and a fixed clock, so two calls are byte-identical (test_short_block_is_deterministic); injection increments uses once per injected record per call via memorypack.touch_used, which is the frozen 15.2 rule, and the rendered uses counter is what the second call then shows - the selection and ordering never change. Budget: injected_budget now subtracts index_bytes + short_bytes (test_injected_budget_pays_for_the_short_block asserts both the short and empty-store cases), so index + short + pack <= PACK_BUDGET_BYTES and AlwaysOnBudgetKb is untouched; the 600-byte and 5-entry sub-caps are enforced by dropping lines that would overspend (test_short_block_clips_every_body_to_160_chars, test_short_block_caps_at_five_entries). Concurrency/shared writes: one writer per file - capture takes the role memory pen with strict=False so a peer lease degrades to skipping the note instead of failing the reconcile, and it never touches LongTermMemory.md, ArchivedMemory.md or the promotion rule (M23-B). Scope: src/teamwork/memorypack.py, src/teamwork/engine.py (memory_short_block + cmd_load), src/teamwork/lanes.py (capture_short_layer, _task_branch_head, build_packet), tests/unit/test_memory_short_layer.py; no docs, no config.py (sibling lanes own the other three constants), no gate, no test weakened.
